podcast.body: Blur's first album, released in the early 1990s, is seen by some critics as the beginning of Britpop and by others as the final phase of the Manchester movement, marking a key transition point between the two genres. "tenemos ese primer disco de Blur que hay quien lo cataloga a inicio de Britop, hay quien lo cataloga a final del Manchester"

Released a few months after their first single "She's So High", this debut album was complicated. It sold reasonably well and sounded good for its era, but received very poor critical reviews. Critics largely dismissed it as an attempt to prolong the dying Manchester movement, seeing it as a record label's pressure to stretch a failing trend, and if classified, it belonged more to the Madchester sound than to Britpop, with influences from bands like The Stone Roses.

This debut album was discovered by independent label Food Records in 1990. It is described as a late entry into the Manchester movement, rather than Britpop, but it achieved considerable success within the United Kingdom and garnered significant attention. "Laser no es un disco de Britop, es que hace un disco tardío del movimiento Matchester, que bueno acabó de generando bastante éxito dentro del Reino Unido y llamó bastante la atención."
